summary: This is a well-executed, security-conscious first slice of a support-session (act-on-behalf-of-customer) capability. I independently verified the architectural claims against the live repo rather than trusting the self-report: the raw `db` client used for cross-org writes does in fact bypass RLS (DATABASE_URL/postgres role vs. app_runtime's APP_RUNTIME_DATABASE_URL), matching the established autoProvisionUser/org-provisioning-service.ts precedent; the new support_sessions RLS migration exactly mirrors drizzle/0219's FORCE RLS + app_runtime_org_scoped/service_role_bypass shape; token hashing reuses hashSHA256 from api-keys.ts with a high-entropy (192-bit) token; the end-session update uses an atomic WHERE ended_at IS NULL...RETURNING to avoid a TOCTOU race; and the new audit_logs columns are additive/nullable and backward compatible. I re-ran the suite independently: tsc --noEmit produced 0 errors and `bun test` on the new file passed all 12 assertions, corroborating the self-report. Authorization on all four routes is correctly scoped (veridian_admin-only start, veridian_admin OR the target org's own admin for end, target org's own admin for the on-my-org list). The whoami-target route accepting only a bearer token with no session auth matches this codebase's existing API-key bearer convention (api-key-auth.ts), so it isn't a novel hole. My reservations are scope/completeness, not correctness or security: (1) this PR ships only the plumbing plus one read-only proof route (whoami-target) -- it does not yet let a support agent actually perform impersonated writes across the rest of the app's ERP/compliance modules, so 'session impersonation' as a usable support tool is not complete, only its audited foundation is; (2) the migration has not been applied to any live database yet (no DATABASE_URL/Supabase MCP available to the authoring session), so this is inert until a session with DB access runs it. Given tier2, this requires human sign-off regardless; I recommend the human reviewer confirm they're OK merging foundational infrastructure now versus waiting for a follow-up PR that wires impersonation into real write paths.
issues: Scope: only a read-only demo endpoint (whoami-target) exists to prove the mechanism -- no actual impersonated write capability across ERP/compliance module routes is implemented yet, despite the task title implying broader 'impersonation'

drizzle/0224_support_sessions.sql has not been applied to any live database from this session (no DATABASE_URL/Supabase MCP available) -- must be applied via db:push/Supabase MCP before this feature is functional
No admin-facing endpoint to list all active support sessions across orgs (e.g. for a veridian_admin's own dashboard/oversight) -- only the target org's own admin can list sessions against their org
reason field on POST /api/support-sessions/start has no max-length validation
